claims.text: Microsoft announced Agent Framework on 1 Oct 2025 and shipped 1.0 for .NET and Python on 3 Apr 2026; Go support is in public preview.
The AutoGen repository now reads "Project archived and no longer maintained", and the Semantic Kernel README says Semantic Kernel is now Microsoft Agent Framework.
LangChain and LangGraph reached 1.0 on 22 Oct 2025 with a promise of no breaking changes until 2.0.
LangChain's create_agent now runs on the LangGraph runtime, and langgraph.prebuilt is deprecated in favour of langchain.agents.
Google open-sourced the Agent Development Kit on 9 Apr 2025 and made ADK Python 2.0, with a graph-based workflow runtime, generally available on 19 May 2026.
The OpenAI Agents SDK is still on 0.x releases (Python 0.24.0 on 15 Oct 2026) and is the successor to OpenAI's experimental Swarm.
AWS released Strands Agents 1.0 on 15 Jul 2025 and uses it to power the AgentCore harness, which went GA on 17 Jun 2026.
AgentCore Runtime runs each session in its own microVM, and Google Agent Runtime was formerly called Agent Engine.
Foundry hosted agents and AgentCore Runtime both accept several frameworks, so the choice of cloud does not force the choice of framework.
MCP (agent to tool), A2A (agent to agent) and OpenTelemetry (traces and metrics) are the open protocols at the edges that make agents portable between frameworks and runtimes.

LangGraph is categorized as an orchestration runtime whose control model is explicit nodes, edges, state transitions and checkpoints, suited to complex, durable workflows mixing deterministic and model-directed steps.
The OpenAI Agents SDK uses a model-directed loop with handoffs, agents-as-tools and code orchestration, and fits OpenAI-first applications needing a small set of composable primitives.
Google ADK offers LLM agents, workflow agents, graph workflows and dynamic workflows, and fits Google Cloud, Gemini, multimodal, MCP and A2A-oriented systems.
Microsoft Agent Framework combines agents, graph workflows, middleware, handoffs and typed routing, targeting Microsoft and Azure teams needing enterprise integration and explicit workflows.
CrewAI combines role-based crews with stateful flows, suited to workflows that benefit from distinct roles, delegation and coordinated agents.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is classed as a managed runtime or platform providing hosted infrastructure to deploy, scale, secure, observe and govern agents built with one or more frameworks.
AgentCore documentation shows examples of running agents built with Strands Agents, LangGraph, Google ADK and the OpenAI Agents SDK.

Managed hyperscaler agent runtimes include AWS Bedrock AgentCore, Google Vertex AI Agent Engine and Azure AI Foundry Agent Service, while LangGraph Platform and OpenAI AgentKit are framework-native platforms.

Microsoft Agent Framework is the unified successor to AutoGen and Semantic Kernel, with graph-based workflows, responsible AI guardrails available through Azure AI Foundry, and Python and .NET runtimes at 1.0 GA.
Google ADK is Apache 2.0 licensed and described as an opinionated, batteries-included agent runtime with built-in debugging UIs for GCP-native teams.
The OpenAI Agents SDK is MIT licensed and is positioned for tightly scoped assistants and clean multi-agent delegation with minimal abstraction.
CrewAI is MIT licensed and is positioned for rapid prototyping of role-based multi-agent workflows.
OpenAI is shutting down its visual Agent Builder on 30 November 2026, and AWS closed the original Bedrock Agents to new customers on 30 July 2026.
Google renamed Vertex AI, and OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, LangChain and AWS each launched a hosted agent runtime in 2026; LangGraph is paired with LangSmith Deployment.

The OpenAI Agents SDK's main abstraction is the agent and runner, handling repeated model/tool execution and handoffs, while deployment, tool implementations, storage and approval policy remain the application's responsibility.
